meta.title: Data Analytics Documents
meta.description: DDD documentation framework for Data Analytics. AI reads this file and generates .md files covering KPI definition, metric logic, data pipelines, dashboards, and governance.
meta.applicable_when: Building the analytics layer over an existing operational system — a shared KPI definition, the metric logic that computes it, the pipelines that feed it, and the dashboards and reports people act on. Distinct from the postgresql-design template, which specifies the PostgreSQL schema itself rather than the metrics computed over it; from the web-app template, whose TRACKING_PLAN.md is the declared upstream producer of the events this template consumes via PIPELINE_SPEC.md's source_systems and DATA_CONTRACT.md's upstream_event_contract; and from the ai-workflow template, which produces a recurring generated artifact rather than a governed metrics layer. This template assumes a warehouse-and-BI stack, not a streaming-first one.

agent_instructions.role: You are a data analytics documentation generator. Read this file and produce each document listed in phases[], in dependency order.
agent_instructions.generation_order_strategy: Topological sort by depends_on graph. Business-layer documents (KPI, Metric Spec) have no dependencies and are generated first. Visualization design spec bridges stakeholders and metrics into dashboard standards. Governance and AI docs are generated last. Each document is the canonical source for its concerns — downstream docs reference upstream docs by document ID. Enum values are defined once in their owner document and only indexed in BUSINESS_GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry — downstream documents reference an enum by name, never redefine its values.
agent_instructions.content_language: Write document content in Thai for narrative sections; use English for all identifiers, SQL, field names, table names, and technical terms.
agent_instructions.quality_gate: Each document must cover all sections[] listed. Validate that cross-references (refs[]) resolve to real document IDs before finishing. Metric definitions must be consistent across KPI Dictionary, Metric Spec, and Metric Logic. For each dashboard chart, verify chart type matches viz_design_spec.chart_type_matrix. Gate visualization complexity against the audience: intermediate-level charts (heatmap, scatter, crosshair) require data_literacy_level >= intermediate, and advanced ones (animated, multi-axis, custom) require advanced — matching the complexity levels VIZ_DESIGN_SPEC.md defines. Every metric, dataset, quality rule and dashboard must be documented exactly once in its canonical doc and referenced elsewhere — no duplicate definitions. Never hardcode the adopting organization's own name, its customers, or its domains — use placeholders so the template stays reusable; naming the warehouse, BI and transformation tools the stack actually uses is expected. Every enum is defined in exactly one owner document and only indexed in BUSINESS_GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry — other documents reference it, never redefine it. Never invent a default for a value that needs calibration (quality threshold, anomaly bound, freshness tolerance, retention period, cost ceiling, model acceptance threshold, scale projection, project budget) — declare it null with its calibration source and owner instead.
domain_specific_notes: KPI ≠ metric ≠ dimension — a KPI is the business outcome someone is accountable for (KPI_DICTIONARY.md), a metric is a specific computed number that moves it (METRIC_SPEC.md), and a dimension is what you slice either one by (DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md). A metric with no parent KPI measures something nobody owns; a dimension promoted to a metric produces a number with no formula.

Freshness ≠ completeness ≠ correctness — freshness is whether the data arrived on time (SLA_FRESHNESS.md), completeness is whether all the rows that should exist do (DATA_QUALITY.md), and correctness is whether the computed number is right (TESTING_STRATEGY.md metric validation). A dashboard can be perfectly fresh, perfectly complete and still wrong, and each failure needs a different alert and a different owner.

Data contract ≠ quality rule ≠ test — the contract is the agreement with the producer about what they will send (DATA_CONTRACT.md), a quality rule is what we check on arrival and how the pipeline reacts (DATA_QUALITY.md), and a test is what runs in CI against known inputs (TESTING_STRATEGY.md). Collapsing them means a producer breaking the contract looks identical to our own transformation breaking.

Lineage ≠ impact analysis ≠ changelog — lineage records where a number came from, impact analysis answers what breaks if an upstream thing changes, and the changelog records what actually changed and when. LINEAGE.md owns the first two and ANALYTICS_CHANGELOG.md the third; a lineage graph with no changelog cannot explain why yesterday's number differs from today's.

The business glossary is the naming authority. A term defined in BUSINESS_GLOSSARY.md determines the metric name in METRIC_SPEC.md, the column name in DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md and the label on the dashboard. When they disagree, the glossary wins and the others are corrected.

A metric definition change is a breaking change. Restating a number that has already been reported is not a bug fix — it needs a changelog entry, a stated effective date, and a decision about whether history is restated or the old definition is kept alongside. ANALYTICS_CHANGELOG.md owns that record.

PDPA is the compliance frame throughout this template, not GDPR. Personal data reaches the warehouse through pipelines, survives in extracts, dashboards, and model training sets, and an erasure request must reach all of them — not only the source table.

Every KPI must be computable from data that actually lands. A KPI whose inputs no pipeline produces is an aspiration, not a measurement — the coverage check belongs in the readiness gates, not in a later conversation.

Project delivery budget and go-live date (CONSTRAINTS.md) ≠ ongoing monthly cost ceiling (DATA_GOVERNANCE.md cost_governance) ≠ per-query cost guard rails (DATA_GOVERNANCE.md) — CONSTRAINTS.md owns what must be true before launch; DATA_GOVERNANCE.md owns what must stay true in operation.

description.en: Fixed, pre-launch constraints — platform, scale, compliance, budget, and integration.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CONSTRAINTS.md documenting every fixed, pre-launch constraint the analytics build must respect. Cover: (1) platform and tooling — the mandatory warehouse, BI tool with its licensing tier and seat limit, transform tool, and any required connector; (2) scale — data volume projected at 1yr/3yr for the fastest-growing fact table, source API rate limits, and warehouse concurrent-query/connection quotas; (3) compliance and residency — data residency region, legal basis for collection, and any industry standard, distinct from the ongoing retention and access-control rules DATA_GOVERNANCE.md owns; (4) project budget and timeline — the one-time delivery budget ceiling and go-live date, distinct from DATA_GOVERNANCE.md's ongoing monthly cost ceiling; (5) integration constraints — required source-system integrations and how stable each one's contract is expected to be.
agent_hints.input_context: Gather from stakeholder interviews, the project brief, and existing vendor contracts. These constraints are inputs to PIPELINE_SPEC.md's platform choice and DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md's scale assumptions.
agent_hints.validation: Every constraint must be stated so it can be checked — a measurable threshold, a named standard, or an explicit yes/no condition. Any threshold not yet calibrated must be null with a named calibration owner. Compliance and budget items must not restate DATA_GOVERNANCE.md's retention, access-control, or cost-ceiling content — this document owns what must be true before launch, DATA_GOVERNANCE.md owns what must stay true in operation.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a BUSINESS_GLOSSARY.md that defines all business terms used in data analysis and reporting. For each term include: the official definition, why it is commonly misunderstood, and the authoritative source. Pay special attention to terms like 'Active Customer', 'Churn', 'Revenue' (booked vs collected), 'MRR', and any org-specific terminology.
agent_hints.input_context: Source terms from KPI definitions, metric names, and any known internal disputes about what a word means. This document reduces cross-team confusion. The Enumeration Registry section is the single index of every enum used across the template — data_literacy_level (STAKEHOLDERS.md), scd_type and pdpa_classification (DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md), rule_severity (DATA_QUALITY.md), chart_type and complexity_level (VIZ_DESIGN_SPEC.md), model_status (AI_MODEL_SPEC.md), change_type (ANALYTICS_CHANGELOG.md) metric_status (METRIC_SPEC.md), data_need_priority (STAKEHOLDERS.md), dataset_criticality (SLA_FRESHNESS.md), work_item_status (TASKS.md) and incident_severity (RUNBOOK.md). This document is generated third, before most of those exist, so the registry starts as the intended owner map and is reconciled on a second pass once the owner documents are written. This document indexes; it never redefines a value owned elsewhere.
agent_hints.validation: Each term must have: term, official_definition, common_misunderstanding, authoritative_source. Disputed terms section must address at least 3 commonly confused concepts. The Enumeration Registry must map every enum listed in input_context to exactly one owner document and contain zero enum values.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a DATA_CONTRACT.md defining the interface contract between the Product team (data producers) and the Data team (data consumers). For each event or table in the contract include: schema definition, required vs optional fields, data types, allowed values, and the SLA (latency and availability). Define a breaking change policy including versioning and migration notice period. If an upstream web-app TRACKING_PLAN.md exists, add an Upstream Event Contract section: the event contract this pipeline consumes, the event_schema_version this document assigns to each consumed event (independent of this document's own Contract Version, and distinct because TRACKING_PLAN.md itself carries no schema_version of its own), and how a shape change with no upstream version bump is detected.
agent_hints.input_context: Depends on data_model_spec for table and field definitions. Critical for AI automation — any downstream pipeline or model depends on this contract being stable. If a web-app TRACKING_PLAN.md exists upstream, its event_name enum is the source of the events named in the Upstream Event Contract section — cite the enum, never re-list its values. TRACKING_PLAN.md carries no schema_version of its own; this document is where a version gets assigned to each consumed event, on first ingestion. PIPELINE_SPEC.md and DATA_QUALITY.md are generated after this document — record the intended schema-drift detection mechanism as an expectation here and reconcile it on a second pass once those documents exist.
agent_hints.validation: Every table/event in the contract must have: schema[], required_fields[], data_types[], sla (latency + availability). Breaking change policy must specify notice period and migration procedure. Every SLA figure (latency, availability, completeness percentage) must be a calibrated value with its source, or null with a named calibration owner. If an Upstream Event Contract section is present, every consumed event must have an event_schema_version assigned here — a value independent of this document's own Contract Version — and a named schema-drift detection mechanism, since the producer signals no version of its own.

optional_integrations.description: The Upstream Event Contract section this document declares may optionally take its event names from a web-app TRACKING_PLAN.md instead of an unspecified producer. TRACKING_PLAN.md remains the sole owner of the event_name enum and every value in it — this document cites the enum and never re-lists its values. DATA_CONTRACT.md owns only the event_schema_version it assigns on first ingestion, since TRACKING_PLAN.md carries no schema_version of its own. Optional: this document's contract is complete with any other event producer.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a PIPELINE_SPEC.md documenting every data pipeline. For each pipeline include: source system (database, API, webhook, or a product event stream such as a web-app TRACKING_PLAN.md — ingested as a typed event feed rather than a table pull), transformation steps with tool (dbt, Make, GCP Dataflow, etc.), destination (data warehouse, dashboard), schedule (cron expression), upstream dependencies, and error handling / retry policy. Draw the pipeline DAG using Mermaid. Document credentials and secret management: which secret store holds each connection's credentials, who may read them per environment, the rotation cadence, and the rule that no credential is ever committed to the repo.
agent_hints.input_context: Pipelines must produce all tables defined in DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md. Transformation logic must implement SQL from METRIC_LOGIC.md. RUNBOOK.md and ANALYTICS_CHANGELOG.md are generated later; note the intended runbook scenario and changelog entry here and reconcile on a second pass.
agent_hints.validation: Every table in DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md must have a pipeline that populates it. Each pipeline must have: source, transform_tool, destination, schedule (cron), dependencies[], error_handling. Every connection must name its secret store and rotation cadence — no credential value may appear in the document.

optional_integrations.description: A pipeline's source system may optionally be a web-app TRACKING_PLAN.md — an event-stream ingest of already-typed events — instead of an unspecified source. TRACKING_PLAN.md remains the sole owner of the event_name enum and every event's schema; this document only ingests and routes the events it names, it never redefines what an event means or adds a value to the enum. Optional: this document's source-system list is complete with any other kind of source.

items.text_th: Transient ≠ Permanent — error ชั่วคราว (timeout, rate limit, source ล่มชั่วคราว) retry แล้วมีโอกาสสำเร็จ; error ถาวร (schema เปลี่ยน, credential หมดอายุ, ข้อมูลผิดรูป) retry กี่ครั้งก็ได้ผลเดิม — retry ประเภทหลังคือการเลื่อน alert ออกไปโดยเปล่าประโยชน์

description.th: วิธีโหลดข้อมูลต่อ pipeline — incremental หรือ full, watermark, upsert key และการรันซ้ำอย่างปลอดภัย
description.en: How each pipeline loads — incremental or full, watermark, upsert key, and safe re-runs.

items.text_th: Incremental vs Full Refresh — ต่อ pipeline ระบุว่าโหลดเฉพาะส่วนใหม่หรือสร้างใหม่ทั้งชุด พร้อมเหตุผล — full refresh ที่โตขึ้นเรื่อย ๆ จะพังตอนข้อมูลใหญ่ ส่วน incremental ที่ไม่มี watermark จะพลาดแถวเงียบ ๆ
items.text_en: Incremental vs Full Refresh — per pipeline, whether it loads only new data or rebuilds the whole set, and why; a full refresh that keeps growing breaks once the data is large, and an incremental load with no watermark silently drops rows

items.text_th: Watermark / Cursor — คอลัมน์และค่าที่ใช้บอกว่า 'โหลดถึงไหนแล้ว' (เช่น updated_at, sequence id) และวิธีจัดการเมื่อ source แก้ข้อมูลย้อนหลังโดยไม่ขยับ watermark
items.text_en: Watermark / Cursor — the column and value marking how far the load got (updated_at, a sequence id), and what happens when the source edits history without moving that watermark

items.text_th: Upsert Key + Idempotent Re-run — คีย์ที่ใช้ merge เพื่อให้รันซ้ำแล้วไม่เกิดแถวซ้ำ — pipeline ที่รันซ้ำไม่ได้อย่างปลอดภัย ทำให้การกู้คืนทุกครั้งกลายเป็นการตัดสินใจเสี่ยง; การตรวจว่าไม่เกิดแถวซ้ำเป็น rule ใน DATA_QUALITY.md
items.text_en: Upsert Key + Idempotent Re-run — the merge key that makes a re-run produce no duplicates; a pipeline that cannot be safely re-run turns every recovery into a risky decision; the duplicate-row check that proves it is a DATA_QUALITY.md rule

items.text_th: Backfill Window — ช่วงเวลาที่ backfill ได้, ต้นทุนโดยประมาณ, ลำดับการรัน และผลต่อตัวเลขที่เคยรายงานไปแล้ว (ต้องบันทึกใน ANALYTICS_CHANGELOG.md ถ้าตัวเลขเปลี่ยน)
items.text_en: Backfill Window — how far back a backfill may run, its rough cost, the order it must run in, and its effect on numbers already reported (recorded in ANALYTICS_CHANGELOG.md when they change)

description.th: Validation rules, null checks, range checks และ anomaly detection rules สำหรับ data pipeline
description.en: Validation rules, null checks, range checks, and anomaly detection for data pipelines.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a DATA_QUALITY.md defining all data quality rules. For each rule include: rule name, table/column it applies to, rule type (null check, range check, referential integrity, anomaly), expected behavior, actual SQL assertion, severity (error/warning), and action on failure. Examples: MRR must never be negative; missing org_id is a blocking error; churn rate > 20% triggers an anomaly alert.
agent_hints.input_context: Rules must reference tables in DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md. Rules must protect the metric calculations in METRIC_LOGIC.md from bad input data.
agent_hints.validation: Every fact table in DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md must have at least one quality rule. Rules must specify severity (error = blocks pipeline, warning = alerts only). Every anomaly threshold must be either a number derived from observed history with that source stated, or null with a named calibration owner — never a round figure with nothing behind it.

description.th: ตรวจว่า fields ที่ required ไม่เป็น null และ data ครบถ้วน
description.en: Verify required fields are not null and data is complete.

items.text_th: Required Non-null Fields — fields ที่ต้องไม่ null เช่น org_id, event_date
items.text_en: Required Non-null Fields — fields that must not be null, e.g. org_id, event_date

items.text_th: Completeness Rate — % rows ที่ต้องมี value ครบ (target ที่ calibrate จากข้อมูลจริง หรือ null พร้อม owner)
items.text_en: Completeness Rate — % of rows that must have complete values (target calibrated from observed history, or null with a named owner)

items.text_th: Missing Data Pattern — pattern ของ missing data ที่ต้อง alert เช่น gap ใน time series
items.text_en: Missing Data Pattern — alerting patterns for missing data, e.g. time series gaps

items.text_th: Severity + SQL Assertion + Action — ต่อ rule ระบุ severity (error = หยุด pipeline, warning = แจ้งอย่างเดียว), SQL assertion ที่รันจริง และสิ่งที่เกิดขึ้นเมื่อ fail
items.text_en: Severity + SQL Assertion + Action — per rule: the severity (error blocks the pipeline, warning only alerts), the SQL assertion actually executed, and what happens on failure

description.th: ตรวจว่าค่าอยู่ใน range ที่ valid
description.en: Verify values are within valid ranges.

items.text_th: Numeric Range — เช่น MRR >= 0, churn_rate 0-100%
items.text_en: Numeric Range — e.g. MRR >= 0, churn_rate 0-100%

items.text_th: Enum Validation — ค่า categorical ต้องอยู่ใน allowed values
items.text_en: Enum Validation — categorical values must be in allowed values list

items.text_th: Date Range — dates ต้องไม่อยู่ในอนาคตหรือก่อนวัน company founded
items.text_en: Date Range — dates must not be in the future or before company founding date

items.text_th: Severity + SQL Assertion + Action — ต่อ rule ระบุ severity (error = หยุด pipeline, warning = แจ้งอย่างเดียว), SQL assertion ที่รันจริง และสิ่งที่เกิดขึ้นเมื่อ fail
items.text_en: Severity + SQL Assertion + Action — per rule: the severity (error blocks the pipeline, warning only alerts), the SQL assertion actually executed, and what happens on failure

description.th: ตรวจว่า foreign key relationships ถูกต้อง
description.en: Verify foreign key relationships are valid.

items.text_th: FK Existence — ทุก foreign key ต้อง exist ใน dimension table
items.text_en: FK Existence — every foreign key must exist in the dimension table

items.text_th: Orphan Records — records ที่มี FK ชี้ไปที่ row ที่ไม่มีอยู่
items.text_en: Orphan Records — records with FK pointing to non-existent rows

items.text_th: Cardinality Check — ตรวจ 1:N, N:M relationships ว่าถูกต้อง
items.text_en: Cardinality Check — verify 1:N, N:M relationships are correct

items.text_th: Severity + SQL Assertion + Action — ต่อ rule ระบุ severity (error = หยุด pipeline, warning = แจ้งอย่างเดียว), SQL assertion ที่รันจริง และสิ่งที่เกิดขึ้นเมื่อ fail
items.text_en: Severity + SQL Assertion + Action — per rule: the severity (error blocks the pipeline, warning only alerts), the SQL assertion actually executed, and what happens on failure

items.text_th: Upstream Schema Drift — วิธีจับว่า source เปลี่ยน schema โดยไม่แจ้ง (validate ทุก load เทียบ schema ที่คาดไว้ หรือเทียบ shape hash) และสิ่งที่ทำเมื่อจับได้: หยุด pipeline, กันข้อมูลเข้า warehouse, แจ้งเจ้าของ contract — drift ที่ไม่ถูกจับจะกลายเป็น metric ที่ผิดแบบดูปกติ
items.text_en: Upstream Schema Drift — how an unannounced source schema change is caught (validate each load against the expected schema, or compare a shape hash) and what happens on detection: halt the pipeline, keep the data out of the warehouse, notify the contract owner; undetected drift becomes a wrong metric that looks normal

description.th: Rules สำหรับตรวจจับค่าผิดปกติใน metrics
description.en: Rules for detecting anomalous metric values.

items.text_th: GIST — anomaly rule ที่ตั้ง threshold ไว้แคบเกินจะส่ง alert จนไม่มีใครอ่าน ส่วนที่กว้างเกินจะเงียบตอนที่ควรดัง — threshold ต้องมาจากการดูข้อมูลจริงย้อนหลัง ไม่ใช่ตัวเลขกลม ๆ; ค่าที่ยังไม่ calibrate ให้เป็น null พร้อมเจ้าของ
items.text_en: GIST — an anomaly rule set too tight pages until nobody reads it, and one set too loose stays quiet exactly when it should not; thresholds come from looking at real history rather than from a round number, and any value not yet calibrated is null with a named owner

items.text_th: Threshold-based — เช่น churn rate > 20% หรือ MRR drop > 15%
items.text_en: Threshold-based — e.g. churn rate > 20% or MRR drop > 15%

items.text_th: Statistical — ค่าที่เกิน เช่น 3 standard deviations ที่ calibrate จากข้อมูลจริง จาก rolling average
items.text_en: Statistical — values exceeding e.g. 3 standard deviations, calibrated from observed history from rolling average

items.text_th: Volume-based — row count เปลี่ยนแปลงมากกว่า 30% จาก previous run
items.text_en: Volume-based — row count changes by more than a calibrated share, e.g. 30% from previous run

items.text_th: Alert Configuration — severity level และ notification channel ต่อ rule — ค่า severity คือ enum rule_severity ที่เอกสารนี้เป็นเจ้าของ
items.text_en: Alert Configuration — severity level and notification channel per rule — severity values are the rule_severity enum owned by this document

description.th: Refresh frequency, delay tolerance และ alert rules สำหรับทุก pipeline และ dashboard
description.en: Refresh frequency, delay tolerance, and alert rules for all pipelines and dashboards.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate an SLA_FRESHNESS.md specifying data freshness requirements. For each dataset or dashboard include: required refresh frequency, maximum acceptable delay (delay tolerance), the measurement window, alert threshold (when to page on-call), and the escalation procedure. Distinguish between business-critical datasets (e.g. MRR) and informational datasets.
agent_hints.input_context: Freshness requirements must be consistent with PIPELINE_SPEC.md schedules. Alert thresholds inform the monitoring configuration. DASHBOARD_SPEC.md and RUNBOOK.md are generated later; record the intended dashboard dependency and escalation target here and reconcile on a second pass.
agent_hints.validation: Every pipeline in PIPELINE_SPEC.md must have a freshness SLA entry. Each entry must have: refresh_frequency, delay_tolerance, alert_threshold, escalation_contact. Every delay tolerance and alert threshold must be a calibrated value with its source, or null with a named calibration owner.

description.th: SLA ด้าน freshness ของ data แต่ละชุด
description.en: Data freshness SLA for each dataset.

items.text_th: Freshness ≠ Completeness ≠ Correctness — freshness คือข้อมูลมาถึงตรงเวลาไหม; completeness คือแถวที่ควรมีอยู่ครบไหม; correctness คือตัวเลขที่คำนวณออกมาถูกไหม — dashboard สดและครบแต่ผิดได้ และสามอย่างนี้ต้องมี alert คนละตัวและเจ้าของคนละคน
items.text_en: Freshness ≠ Completeness ≠ Correctness — freshness is whether the data arrived on time, completeness whether every row that should exist does, correctness whether the computed number is right; a dashboard can be fresh and complete and still wrong, and each needs its own alert and owner

description.th: กลยุทธ์ testing สำหรับ data pipelines, dbt models, metric calculations และ dashboard outputs
description.en: Testing strategy for data pipelines, dbt models, metric calculations, and dashboard outputs.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a TESTING_STRATEGY.md for the data analytics stack. Cover: (1) Unit tests — dbt schema tests, singular tests, and custom SQL assertions per table; (2) Integration tests — end-to-end pipeline runs verifying row counts and metric values against expected output; (3) Metric validation — cross-check metric outputs against METRIC_SPEC.md formulas using sample data; (4) Dashboard acceptance tests — verify chart renders, filters work, and numbers match pipeline output; (5) CI/CD integration — when tests run, what blocks deployment. Reference DATA_QUALITY.md rules as the baseline for test assertions.
agent_hints.input_context: Tests must cover every quality rule in DATA_QUALITY.md. Metric validation tests must reference METRIC_LOGIC.md SQL. Test automation must integrate with the pipeline orchestration tool. DASHBOARD_SPEC.md is generated later — write the acceptance tests against the dashboards planned in METRIC_SPEC.md coverage and reconcile once DASHBOARD_SPEC.md exists.
agent_hints.validation: Every fact table in data_model_spec must have at least one test. Metric validation tests must reference metric_logic SQL. CI/CD section must specify what blocks a deployment (failing tests). Coverage expectations must be stated as a number with its rationale, or null with a named calibration owner.

description.th: กำหนด chart type, color theme, interaction pattern และ accessibility guidelines สำหรับทุก dashboard — bridge ระหว่าง stakeholders/metric_spec กับ dashboard_spec
description.en: Define chart types, color theme, interaction patterns, and accessibility guidelines for all dashboards — bridging stakeholders/metric_spec to dashboard_spec.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a VIZ_DESIGN_SPEC.md that bridges stakeholder needs and metric shapes into concrete visualization standards. (1) Build a chart_type_matrix mapping each metric type (time-series ratio, categorical count, ranking, proportion) to a recommended chart type (line, bar, pie, table, heatmap) with anti-patterns and grain considerations. (2) Define a color_theme_spec with primary/secondary/accent palette, semantic colors (green=positive, red=alert, amber=warning), font rules — then produce a viz_theme.py code block exporting COLOR_PALETTE, FONT_RULES, and CHART_DEFAULTS as a reusable Python module, delivered as a fenced code block inside this document so dashboard code can copy it verbatim into viz_theme.py. (3) Define interaction_spec: tooltip format per chart type, crosshair behavior and cross-chart sync, click-through drill-down targets, animation rules. (4) Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios, colorblind-safe palette variant (protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia), screen reader alt-text and aria-label rules, keyboard navigation. (5) Data Literacy Guard Rails: map visualization complexity levels (basic=bar/line/table, intermediate=heatmap/scatter/crosshair, advanced=animated/multi-axis/custom) to each stakeholder group's data_literacy_level from STAKEHOLDERS.md — gate rule: never render a viz above the audience's literacy level.
agent_hints.input_context: Read STAKEHOLDERS.md for data_literacy_level per consumer group (basic/intermediate/advanced). Read METRIC_SPEC.md for metric types and grain. For chart type selection start from references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-main.md (the decision tree), then read the file for the specific chart before recommending it: references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-line.md, references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-barplot.md, references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-scatter.md, references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-heatmap.md, references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-histogram.md, references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-donut.md (this is the file for pie charts), references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-treemap.md, references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-sankey.md, references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-violin.md and references/data-to-viz/data-to-viz-choropleth.md. Each states when to use the chart, when not to, and the common mistakes — the anti-patterns column of the matrix must come from those files rather than from memory. The wider data-to-viz.com corpus in references/ stays available for chart types outside this list — see references/README.md for the full index. This document must be completed before DASHBOARD_SPEC.md — dashboard builders must import viz_theme.py and follow chart_type_matrix for every chart.
agent_hints.validation: Every metric type in metric_spec must map to a chart type in chart_type_matrix. The viz_theme code block must be valid Python exporting COLOR_PALETTE, FONT_RULES and CHART_DEFAULTS. Every chart type in interaction_spec must have tooltip and drill-down target defined. Data literacy guard rails must cover all three literacy levels (basic/intermediate/advanced) defined in stakeholders.

description.th: คู่มือ on-call สำหรับ pipeline failures, stale data, metric anomalies และ SLA breaches
description.en: On-call guide for pipeline failures, stale data, metric anomalies, and SLA breaches.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a RUNBOOK.md as the on-call reference for the data team. For each common failure scenario include: trigger condition, severity (P0/P1/P2), first-response steps, root cause checklist, recovery procedure, and rollback steps. Scenarios must include: (1) pipeline fails to complete on schedule, (2) data freshness SLA breached, (3) metric value anomaly detected, (4) data quality check failure, (5) dashboard shows stale or missing data. Define escalation contacts and response time SLAs per severity. Include a post-incident review template. Document retention enforcement and archival: the purge and archive jobs that enforce the DATA_GOVERNANCE.md retention policy, cold-storage restore, and how PDPA erasure requests reach archives.
agent_hints.input_context: Failure scenarios must reference PIPELINE_SPEC.md and SLA_FRESHNESS.md. Metric anomaly scenarios must reference DATA_QUALITY.md thresholds.
agent_hints.validation: Must cover at least 5 failure scenarios. Each scenario must have: trigger, severity, first_response_steps[], recovery_procedure, rollback_steps. Escalation contacts must include primary and secondary on-call. Response time SLAs must be specified per severity level. Retention enforcement must name the job that enforces each retention period in DATA_GOVERNANCE.md.

checklist.text_en: Visualization complexity never exceeds the audience's data_literacy_level — intermediate charts (heatmap, scatter, crosshair) only for intermediate or above, animated, multi-axis and custom charts only for advanced
